description: A linter for legal billing statements — catch vague narratives, block billing, math errors and invalid UTBMS codes before the bill goes out

readme.text:
# billing-lint

[![CI](https://github.com/kirillsakhin/billing-lint/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/kirillsakhin/billing-lint/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

A linter for legal billing statements. Point it at a pre-bill export — CSV, XLSX or
LEDES 1998B — and it flags the problems that get invoices cut or bounced back: vague
narratives, block billing, math that doesn't add up, template leftovers, duplicated
entries, invalid UTBMS codes. Deterministically, offline, in CI if you want.

## Why

Anyone who reviews pre-bills knows the drill. The narrative says "attention to file".
Two entries bill the same document review twice. An entry says "Draft letter to
[client name]". Hours × rate doesn't equal the amount. Every one of these costs money
or trust when a client's billing team finds it first.

The obvious 2026 answer is "have an LLM review the statement" — and it works worse
than you'd expect. LLM batch review is inconsistent: the same defect gets flagged in
entry 3 and silently passed in entry 47, and two runs of the same statement disagree
with each other. Reviewing 400 entries in one prompt makes it worse, not better.

So billing-lint does it the other way around. Deterministic rules first: they catch
the same defect every time, in every entry, with no API key, and they can gate a CI
pipeline or a pre-send checklist. The LLM comes second, optionally, and only where it
adds something rules can't — suggesting a better narrative for entries the rules
already flagged.

## Install

```
pip install billing-lint
```

Or `pipx install billing-lint` for the CLI alone. Extras: `billing-lint[xlsx]` for
Excel files, `billing-lint[llm]` for the LLM suggestion pass.

## Quickstart

```
billing-lint check prebill.csv
```

Against the bundled demo statement ([`examples/sample_en.csv`](examples/sample_en.csv)):

```
billing-lint — examples/sample_en.csv
format=csv entries=23 matter_language=en

ERROR   BL001 line 4: amount 500.00 does not match hours × rate = 600.00
ERROR   BL006 line 9: placeholder text in narrative: '[client name]'
ERROR   BL010 line 16: zero or negative hours (0)
WARNING BL002 line 5: vague narrative (matched: 'attention to file')
WARNING BL003 line 6: possible block billing: 3 activities in one 3.5h entry
WARNING BL004 line 7: possibly non-billable activity (matched: 'scanning')
WARNING BL005 line 8: narrative language 'ru' differs from matter language 'en'
WARNING BL007 line 10: narrative names a colleague (Quint); consider a role-based reference
WARNING BL008 line 12: exact duplicate of line 11
WARNING BL008 line 14: near-duplicate of line 13 (similarity 0.83)
WARNING BL009 line 15: unknown task code 'L999'
WARNING BL010 statement: Quint, Leo billed 13.5h on 2026-08-14 (max 12h)
INFO    BL010 statement: 20 of 21 entries are exact multiples of 0.5h — check
that increments reflect actual time
```

For CI or scripting:

```
billing-lint check invoice.ledes --format json --fail-on warning
```

Exit codes: `0` — clean (below the `--fail-on` threshold), `1` — findings at or above
it, `2` — usage or file error. Reports come as `console`, `json` or `md`
(`--output report.md` writes to a file).

## Rules

| ID | Name | Default | What it catches |
|----|------|---------|-----------------|
| BL000 | ledes-structure | error | malformed LEDES 1998B records |
| BL001 | math-integrity | error | hours × rate ≠ amount; line totals ≠ invoice total |
| BL002 | vague-narrative | warning | "attention to file", «работа по делу», one-word narratives |
| BL003 | block-billing | warning | several activities lumped into one long entry |
| BL004 | non-billable-activity | warning | clerical work billed as fees (filing, scanning, invoicing) |
| BL005 | language-mismatch | warning | narrative language ≠ matter language (en/ru) |
| BL006 | placeholder-text | error | `[name]`, TBD, XXX, `{{merge_field}}` on a client bill |
| BL007 | name-in-narrative | warning | colleagues named where a role reference belongs |
| BL008 | duplicate-narrative | warning | exact and near-duplicate entries within a date window |
| BL009 | utbms-validity | warning | unknown L/A/E/B/C/P codes; fee/expense code mismatches; missing required codes |
| BL010 | time-anomalies | warning | zero/negative hours (error), >12h days, suspiciously uniform increments (info) |

`billing-lint rules` prints this list; every threshold and severity is configurable.

**Honest limits.** BL003 is a heuristic — it splits the narrative on separators and
counts activity verbs, and it will sometimes be wrong in both directions. BL007 builds
its name list from the statement's own timekeepers (no NER, no external data), so it
only knows the people on the bill plus any `extra_names` you configure. Russian
surname inflection («обсуждение с Соколовой») defeats exact matching — a known v1
limit. Rule IDs are stable API: they never get renumbered, so you can pin config and
CI checks to them.

## Input formats

- **CSV** — headers are matched against a synonym table in English and Russian
  (`Description`/`Описание`, `Hours`/`Часы`, …). Anything nonstandard maps explicitly
  via `input.columns` in config. Decimal commas (`1,5`) parse fine. Minimum viable
  columns: a narrative plus hours or amount.
- **XLSX** — first worksheet, same mapping (`pip install "billing-lint[xlsx]"`).
- **LEDES 1998B** — the 24-field e-billing format. Structure is validated (BL000),
  the invoice total is reconciled (BL001), and task/activity codes are required
  (BL009) as the format intends.
- Dates: ISO (`2026-08-05`), LEDES (`20260805`), European dotted (`05.08.2026`), and
  slash dates read as US `MM/DD/YYYY`.

## Configuration

`billing-lint init` writes a starter `.billing-lint.yaml`. Everything is optional:

```yaml
matter_language: auto   # en | ru | auto (majority vote of narratives)
fail_on: error          # exit 1 at or above this severity

input:
  format: auto          # auto | csv | ledes
  columns:              # only what the synonym table can't guess
    narrative: "Line Description"

rules:
  BL007:
    enabled: false      # your firm doesn't mind names in narratives
  BL008:
    similarity_threshold: 0.7
    date_window_days: 3
  BL009:
    require_codes: true # force UTBMS codes even for CSV input
  BL010:
    max_daily_hours: 10

llm:
  model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
  max_entries: 50
  timeout_seconds: 60
```

Unknown keys are errors, not silent ignores — a typo in a rule name won't quietly
disable your check.

## LLM pass

```
billing-lint check prebill.csv --llm anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
billing-lint check prebill.csv --llm default        # uses llm.model from config
```

The model only sees entries the deterministic rules already flagged (capped at
`llm.max_entries`), and returns a suggested rewrite per entry, shown in the report.
Any model [litellm](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm) supports works — Anthropic,
OpenAI, a local Ollama model. Two guardrails are built in: a suggestion containing
placeholder text (`[name of court]` and friends) is withheld rather than shown, and
if the pass fails part-way the report says so prominently instead of pretending it
ran.

**Privacy:** without `--llm`, nothing ever leaves your machine. With it, only the
flagged narratives and their findings go to the provider you chose.

## Roadmap

More languages (the wordlists are plain YAML — PRs welcome), LEDES XML 2.x, more
UTBMS code sets, configurable date-order parsing. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to add a rule or a language.
